title: Impact of Hospital Choice on 30-Day Mortality

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Instrumental Variables (IV) approach using ambulance diversion (z) as an instrument for hospital choice (x) to estimate the causal effect on 30-day mortality (y). The key assumptions are: (1) Relevance: ambulance diversion affects hospital choice, (2) Exclusion restriction: ambulance diversion only affects mortality through its effect on hospital choice, and (3) Exogeneity: ambulance diversion is as-good-as-random conditional on controls.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s82_data.csv")

# Check data structure
print("Data summary:")
print(summary(data))

# First stage: Check instrument relevance
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
print("\nFirst Stage Results:")
print(summary(first_stage))

# F-statistic for weak instruments test
f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
print(paste("\nFirst Stage F-statistic:", round(f_stat, 3)))
print(paste("Weak instrument concern if F < 10:", f_stat < 10))

# Reduced form: Direct effect of instrument on outcome
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
print("\nReduced Form Results:")
print(summary(reduced_form))

# Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS)
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
print("\nIV (2SLS) Results:")
print(summary(iv_model))

# Extract key coefficient
iv_coeff <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
iv_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(iv_model)))["x"]
print(paste("\nKey Result - Hospital Choice Effect on 30-day Mortality:"))
print(paste("Coefficient:", round(iv_coeff, 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(iv_se, 4)))
print(paste("95% CI: [", round(iv_coeff - 1.96*iv_se, 4), ",", round(iv_coeff + 1.96*iv_se, 4), "]"))

# OLS comparison (biased but useful for comparison)
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
ols_coeff <- coef(ols_model)["x"]
print(paste("\nOLS Coefficient (for comparison):", round(ols_coeff, 4)))

# Robustness checks

# 1. Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors
robust_se <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(iv_model, type = "HC1")))["x"]
print(paste("\nRobust Standard Error:", round(robust_se, 4)))

# 2. Test for endogeneity (Hausman test)
hausman_test <- summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)
print("\nDiagnostic Tests:")
print(hausman_test$diagnostics)

# 3. Overidentification test (would need more instruments)
print("\nNote: Overidentification test requires multiple instruments (not applicable here)")

# 4. Different control specifications
iv_no_controls <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = data)
no_controls_coeff <- coef(iv_no_controls)["x"]
print(paste("\nSensitivity - IV without controls:", round(no_controls_coeff, 4)))

print("\nInterpretation: The coefficient represents the change in 30-day mortality")
print("probability associated with a one-unit change in hospital choice.")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a negative coefficient (around -0.3 to -0.5), indicating that better hospital choice (higher x values) reduces 30-day mortality rates. This makes economic sense as ambulance diversion likely redirects patients from overcrowded/lower-quality facilities to better-performing hospitals. The IV estimate should be larger in magnitude than OLS due to measurement error attenuation bias in the endogenous regressor. The first-stage should show a strong positive relationship between ambulance diversion and hospital choice.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use ambulance diversion as an instrument for hospital choice.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Hospital choice significantly impacts 30-day mortality rates.
